speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
text: asked the Minister for Health (a) what is the justification for the impending increase in MediShield Life premiums; and (b) what strategies are being deployed to control escalating healthcare costs.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
text: asked the Minister for Health (a) in the last 20 years, how much have daily ward charges and daily treatment fees in public hospitals increased; (b) how much have prices of standard drugs, tests and investigations increased in the same period; and (c) based on the proposed revisions to MediShield Life, how much is the expected real increase in MediShield Life coverage, net of medical cost inflation.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: asked the Minister for Health for Singaporeans who are retrenched or self-employed with significantly reduced income during this period, both of whom will be concerned about their MediSave sufficiency to cover the increases in MediShield premiums for the years ahead, whether the Ministry will review and supplement targeted subsidies to ensure that there are no further financial hardship to these groups.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
text: asked the Minister for Health whether he can elaborate about the Government's plans to support persons who are not able to afford the increase in MediShield Life premiums even after subsidies.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The key word here is universal and lifelong.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: It has strengthened our larger healthcare financing framework to keep healthcare affordable, together with Government subsidies, MediSave and MediFund.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Again, it is the 3M + S, that I said so earlier, in the previous question.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: To ensure that the scheme remains sustainable and relevant to Singaporeans, the MediShield Life Council has recently proposed enhancements to benefits and adjustments to premiums.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Ms Foo Mee Har and Mr Liang Eng Hwa asked about the reasons for the premium increases, while Mr Gerald Giam asked about the assumptions behind the premium pricing.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Premiums have been kept unchanged for the first five years of MediShield Life, in line with our earlier public commitment.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: They need to be adjusted to ensure that the MediShield Life Fund remains solvent and sustainable so that it can meet its obligations to all policyholders.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Premiums are priced by actuaries based on established actuarial principles, taking into account claims experience such as utilisation rates and cost of medical treatment, scheme benefits, amongst many other factors.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: There are three key drivers of the premium increases, which I will now elaborate.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Since its launch, MediShield Life has been providing more payouts and greater protection for more Singaporeans.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Mr Xie Yao Quan asked about the growth in hospital charges over the last 20 years.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: This growth in utilisation and payout accounts for about two-third of the premium increases.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: One-quarter of the premium increase is from refreshing the claim limits to ensure that Singaporeans continue to be adequately covered for the majority of subsidised bills.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The remaining portion of the premium increase, which is about just under 10%, supports the benefit enhancements including those implemented since 2018, such as the extension of coverage to inpatient hospices and serious pregnancy complications.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: As premiums are priced taking into account multiple factors, which inevitably vary from country to country, it would not be appropriate to compare MediShield Life's premium increases with other national health insurance schemes, which Mr Leong Mun Wai suggested.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: It would also not be meaningful to compute how much premiums a Singaporean will need to pay over his lifetime, simply by assuming a fixed compounding factor each year.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Future premiums would depend on how the underlying drivers, which I have just illustrated, evolve.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: And this depends on many factors including what we can achieve together to manage healthcare cost.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The amount of premium subsidies an individual would receive will also vary over his lifetime, depending on his financial circumstances.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Several Members including Ms Ng Ling Ling and Mr Yip Hon Weng asked about the support for those who face difficulties with their premiums.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Several financial support schemes are available to ensure that no Singaporean will lose their MediShield Life coverage, or be denied access to appropriate care, just because of an inability to pay their premiums.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: To ensure premiums remain affordable, the Government provides premium subsidies of up to 50% for lower and middle income households.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: All Merdeka Generation seniors receive additional subsidies of up to 10% on top of these premium subsidies and all Pioneer Generation seniors receive special subsidies of up to 60%.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: For the elderly aged 65 and above, the contribution from the Government is even higher, at about 50% of their premiums.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: To illustrate this, the revised premium for a 62-year-old lower income Merdeka Generation or MG senior is $1,020 before subsidies.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: This is the annual premium, which therefore equates to less than $90 a month.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: After taking into account the premium subsidies and additional MG subsidies, the net premium payable per year is $663, or about $55 a month.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Additionally, the MG senior will receive annual MediSave top-ups of $200 for MGs from 2019 to 2023, which can be used to pay for his premiums.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: After this additional $200 offset, the effective premium payable for this MG senior will be $463 a year, or less than $40 a month.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Premiums can be fully paid for by MediSave and the vast majority of Singaporeans have sufficient MediSave for their premiums.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Family members can also utilise their MediSave to help pay the premiums for their loved ones.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Singaporeans who continue to face difficulties even after subsidies and have limited family support can apply for Additional Premium Support or APS.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: This includes those who are mid-way through medical treatment or have experienced a recent job loss or a reduction in income, as pointed out by Ms Ng and Mr Yip.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Certainly, a concern that many Singaporeans have during this COVID-19 crisis.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: If approved, Additional Premium Support will cover all outstanding premiums as well as their future premiums.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The Government had considered deferring the MediShield Life review and consequent premium increases given the current difficult economic situation with COVID-19.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: However, I must emphasise that it was important that MediShield Life remains solvent and sustainable so that it can meet its obligations in time to come when policyholders make claims.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Its coverage also has to be updated and enhanced to remain relevant to the healthcare needs of Singaporeans.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The MediShield Life Council therefore recommended that premiums should be adjusted accordingly.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Nonetheless, in recognition of the challenges faced, the Council further recommended that the Government should provide additional subsidies to help Singaporeans during this exceptional period.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The MediShield Life Fund has to be self-sustaining and based on sound actuarial principles.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Premiums collected have to cover potential current and future claims, including amounts set aside to support future commitments as well as provide a buffer against unforeseen contingencies such as unexpected spikes in hospitalisations due to disease outbreaks.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: As policyholders age, claims are likely to increase and so will premiums.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: A key feature in the MediShield Life scheme is to distribute premiums more evenly throughout the policyholders' lifetimes.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Part of the premiums paid by policyholders during their working ages are set aside to provide for future premium rebates, which will help to moderate premium increases in their older ages.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: This constitutes the bulk of future commitments set aside in the reserves.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: As the majority of policyholders are relatively young today, the amount set aside has been increasing.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Other commitments include future payouts for diseases currently under treatment and will require multi-year care, such as renal failure and cancer.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: This comprises $4.4 billion in premiums collected from policyholders, and $3.1 billion from the Government in terms of premium subsidies and other forms of premium support provided to keep premiums affordable, which also went into the Fund.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: In this same period, a total of $3.5 billion in claims were paid out, while $3 billion was set aside for future premium rebates.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Mr Yip asked about the surplus or loss ratio of the MediShield Life Fund.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: This means that the total premiums collected was slightly less than the total monies required to ensure that the Fund is able to meet current claims and future commitments.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Mr Leong asked about the formula for computing the Fund’s reserves.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The reserves are computed by external professional actuaries in accordance with the Monetary Authority of Singapore or MAS’s requirements and in line with industry standards.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: For more details, the Member can refer to the Insurance (Valuation and Capital) Regulations 2004.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: MediShield Life, I must emphasise, is a not-for-profit Scheme.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: All premiums collected are placed in the MediShield Life Fund which are used solely for the benefit of policyholders and in the administration of the Scheme.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Information about the Fund size, reserves and Incurred Loss Ratio is published on the MOH website.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The financial accounts for the Fund are also audited by an external auditor and submitted to Parliament every year for transparency.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Mr Yip asked whether Singaporeans can pay premiums based on the choice of coverage and illnesses covered.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: MediShield Life focuses on the basic needs of Singaporeans and apply equally to all policyholders.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Those who prefer to have better coverage and are willing to pay higher premiums can consider private Integrated Shield Plans or IPs.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Together, appropriate care can remain affordable for all Singaporeans.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: He mentioned a number of factors that were key in driving the premium increase including medical inflation and so on.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: This is to allow a level of transparency of factors when MediShield Life premium increase.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: The second question also touches on a number of points that the Senior Minister of State mentioned.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: To me, the best way to control healthcare cost is for the population not to fall sick in the first place by staying healthy.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: As MediShield Life premiums are universal and their contributions mandated, how can the healthcare system evolve to a model where Singaporeans are incentivised to live a healthy lifestyle, perhaps by enjoying lower premiums based on the individuals' history of healthy living habits and lower consumption of healthcare services?

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: I think these are important questions that may be on the mind of many people and public as well.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Ideally, it would be good to have a single formula that can address some of these various factors that drive inflation and costs, that translates to higher premiums.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: But the difficulty is that year-to-year, decade-to-decade, it is very hard to predict ahead of time what kind of technology will drive clinical practice.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: In the early years, when I was a student, CT scan was not ubiquitous.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: When we see somebody in the A&E, if you get a head injury, the default is just a plain X-ray of the skull.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: That probably cost about maybe $15-$20 to do a skull X-ray, but it does not tell you very much unless you have a bone fracture.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: It cannot tell you there is bleeding inside your brains, whether there is traumatic soft tissue injury.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Today, it is almost unthinkable, just barely 20 years later, that you do not do a CT scan of the head for somebody with a significant head trauma.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: But the cost factor for a CT scan is actually in the range of hundreds of dollars.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: That is easily a 10- or maybe a 100-fold increase in the cost factor.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: But at that point in time, you cannot really factor in just one single thing, a CT scan, the magnitude of utilisation, the pervasiveness and the cost factor from the technology, how it can be applied clinically, because this also depends on clinical guidelines as well.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, as opposed to a transport fare formula, where the parameters and the variables are a little bit more fixed and more predictable, healthcare inflation takes into account many unforeseen kind of variables that will come along the way.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: That magnitude of inflation is something you cannot predict ahead of time and the pervasiveness of the disease prevalence that requires you to use this treatment is again very hard to scope into one formula that addresses a broad spectrum of needs.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The second question on how to incentivise better behaviour.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Today, if you have no good behaviour, you actually have premium loading, which is what most insurers in practice would practise.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: If you have a diagnosis and you want to continue to be covered for the condition or you want to add on a condition that was previously not covered, the insurer will do a premium loading to add on the coverage for the condition.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: In that sense, it is an incentive to be healthy, so that you do not have a premium increase on the individual basis; not necessary a premium rebate, but you do not want to have a premium increase, by keeping healthy.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: In order to encourage our people to adopt a healthy lifestyle and be healthy, there can be other schemes that the Government can do outside of the scope of insurance to encourage good behaviour.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, there are other ways to incentivise good behaviour without distorting the actuarial calculations for a fund that needs to be sustainable and needs to be solvent.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: I asked for the actuarial report because it is key to accurately compute the premiums and benefits.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: It contains mathematical and statistical models designed to evaluate risk and probabilities, which are a bit complex to explain in a reply to a Parliamentary Question.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Has the Government studied how other countries release the actuarial reports for the national insurance schemes?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: It covers calculations for potential and current and future claims and a detailed sensitivity analysis to model how claims will vary in various economic scenarios.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: So, can I urge the Government to release a report like this, so that independent actuaries can analyse it.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: This will go a long way to improve transparency and help Singaporeans understand the calculations behind the MediShield premiums and benefits instead of being asked to take the Government's word for it.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: I think the answer should be do not just take the Government's word for it.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Take the words of the professionals who are experts in this field.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, it is not the Government's word, it is an external auditor who takes a look at the funds and calculate the loss or the surpluses.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, I think this is not just the Government's words, this is based on external experts, external auditors and transparently reported in Parliament.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: But I take the Members point that, over time, we may have to have a better system of looking at how these assumptions, calculations, need to evolve.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: It has only been about four to five years running and we are collecting data as we go along.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Much of the outcomes will have to depend on how the claims have been paid out, what is the actual lived experiences of patients and how much claims and the percentage of bills that are incurred as well.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, over time, we could perhaps engage different consultants to take a look to challenge the assumptions to do another calculation at the appropriate time, to make sure that we are still on track.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: We can also speak to the consultants and see if they are able to publish some of these data in an academic way.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: But again, this will not be something that most lay people will understand.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: As a doctor who has been practising for about 20-odd years, I can tell you what is the saddest thing we see in the clinics.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The saddest thing we see is when you see a poor patient or family who has limited means coming to a hospital for a catastrophic illness and they are devastated by the worries of healthcare bills.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: We will make sure every Singaporean patient has a basic medical insurance to cover them for catastrophic bills.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The second kind of condition which we see many private insurance exclude are actually congenital conditions.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The moment you are born with a congenital condition, you are already disadvantaged for life.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: No insurance will probably take you on unless you are prepared to pay an arm and a leg for a very high premium to get that coverage.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Many of us who have insurance plans will also know that later on in life when you have the means to buy an insurance plan, but you already have a pre-diagnosed condition, the insurance will take you on but exclude those conditions from coverage as well.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: I think these are the important features of MediShield Life that we got to take into account that is different from any other insurance plans out there, especially in the private sector.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, pervasive coverage, all Singaporeans, all disease, conditions, for life.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Again, "for life" is another important feature because many private insurance plans do not cover you beyond a certain age because they know once you reach a certain age, your disease prevalence goes up, your risk of claim goes very high and your chance of a severe illness is very high as well, and nobody wants to provide coverage.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: If we look at how MediShield Life is constructed, therefore, it is a very unique pervasive universal health coverage plan.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: If I were to make a comparison to, say, a healthcare plan from another country, I think it is very hard to find something that is exactly the same.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: But for purpose of comparison, if I can share some premium data from Hong Kong's VHIS, which is Hong Kong's government-backed Voluntary Health Insurance Scheme.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, first it is Hong Kong, which is an Asian country, pretty much similar to Singapore in terms of social construct and healthcare system, which is quite similar, in the British-base kind of healthcare system.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: But bear in mind, this is a voluntary healthcase system.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Or you can work it out – it is about 76% higher on average across the age bands.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, Hong Kong's healthcare insurance system which is voluntary, on average, at least 76% higher than our premiums.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, it is easily close to two times or more.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, even before subsidies, our premiums for universal coverage, for all conditions, for life, no exclusion, is already much cheaper than the one that Hong Kong has.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: But bear in mind that for the older group, especially those which I said is above 90 years old, they belong to the Pioneer Generation group where there is already additional premium subsidies, premium discounts, MediSave top-ups.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Virtually, it is almost a free healthcare insurance for those who are at the extreme end of age range for the Pioneer Generation.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: I hope that gives the Member a clearer idea of the comparisons that we have.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I am heartened to hear that there are various subsidies for the premium increases, including the COVID-19 subsidies.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: As Members of Parliament, as Advisors to the grassroot organisations, as key touchpoints within the community, we hope that all Members in this House, having understood what is being said earlier, would help to communicate this to your residents.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The Ministry will also push out a series of communications through case illustrations, through engagement with the public, through press releases and perhaps also through write-ups in the media to help share some of this information to the public.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, we look forward to your support and continued partnership.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: However, I do not think he has answered the questions we asked.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I think what we are saying is that we need more transparency in the system.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The Member Mr Gerald Giam has also asked for the future liabilities estimation.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: When the data is disclosed, there will be people who are able to make an informed judgement.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: We really need to have more information about the system in order that we come out with more ideas to arrive at a better system in our country.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The situation that is described by the Senior Minister of State is still not quite — Based on the feedback we have received from the ground, the situation of our healthcare system is still a source of a lot of stress to our people.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: As a result, we are here to get more information.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: That is why disclosure and also the affordability are two very important issues.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: If I may ask one additional question here, is that, the various components that the Government has contributed to the MediShield Life Scheme, which was shared just now, about over $3 billion over the last five years, I think that is what the Senior Minister of State said, can we categorise them under pre-existing conditions, low-income and the ageing factor?

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: If possible, what are the respective contribution based on these components?

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Because at the point when MediShield Life was brought in in 2015, the Committee said that the Government will contribute $850 million to support the pre-existing conditions.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: So, one of the key components of the financing of the scheme is that, will the Government continue to finance these pre-existing conditions going forward; and in the past five years, how much was it?

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, that itself is a sizeable commitment from the Government.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The second thing is we do welcome ideas from experts who can actually help us to also refine the Scheme as we go along.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: But bear in mind this is a very new Scheme and we just started for the last four to five years.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: As we go along, we will try and share more data as possible and involve more actuarial consultants to try and help us to look for new possibilities and new ways to look at some of these things.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: But let me just say that for the purpose of transparency, the Member must note that this is not proposed by Government.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: This is an external consultant who proposes the premiums, audited by an external auditor and report this yearly in Parliament where Members get a chance to question about the proportioning of the Fund and the usage.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: I think transparency is not an issue here.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: We will try and work with the actuarial consultants to see whether some of these publications can go on to the academic circles, for people to take a look as well.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: But bear in mind that what you do in academia, what you look at, has to marry with the actual reality.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: As I was explaining earlier to Ms Foo Mee Har's question, some of these conditions are always evolving.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: We know we have an ageing population so the dynamics will change.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Today, we are trying to fight the war of diabetes because we know diabetes leads to many more downstream consequential problems.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: A person may claim for an amputation of a left leg today.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: There is no telling tomorrow next year that he will have amputation of the other leg.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Following, year after that, he may have one kidney failure or two kidney failures and going on to dialysis and following that, a transplant of the kidneys as well.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Some of these things will have to evolve.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: It is not as if is hard-coded in science.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: You cannot just predict so well ahead of time when a person lose his second leg or will have a kidney transplant.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Twenty-odd years as a doctor in the hospital, I have not seen a single patient who has been declined treatment on the account of inability to pay.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: And many of these predate even the era of MediShield Life.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: I can tell you, with MediShield Life, this will provide an even greater cushion and hopefully a lot more comfort to many of these patients.
